steps.body: Measuring the same object in a different unit changes the NUMBER but never the amount. A rope is 3 meters and also 300 centimeters.
steps.narration: Measuring the same object in a different unit changes the NUMBER but never the amount. A rope is 3 meters and also 300 centimeters.

widget.prompt: How many centimeters in 3 meters? Hop one meter at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Two meter-hops reach 200 cm; the rope is three meters long.
Four hops overshoot — three meters is 300 centimeters.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 430, 3 hops land on 460.
widget.successFeedback: 300 — three meter-hops, each worth 100 centimeters. Same rope, bigger number.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — each meter is 100 centimeters, so three of them reach 300.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — three meters stops exactly at 300 centimeters.

predict.prompt: A rope is 3 m. In centimeters, is the number bigger or smaller?
predict.reveal: Centimeters are smaller, so many more of them fit along the same rope — 300 instead of 3.

cml.actionGoal: Hold the quantity fixed while the unit changes, and watch which way the NUMBER moves for g4v unit size.
invariants: Converting never changes how much there is: a smaller unit needs more of them and a bigger unit needs fewer, so the number moves in the opposite direction to the unit size in g4v unit size.
misconceptions: Multiplying when converting to a bigger unit, adding the conversion factor instead of multiplying by it, or comparing bare numbers across different units.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: The same rope is measured in meters and in centimeters. Which measurement has the LARGER number?

options.label: Centimeters use smaller units
options.feedback: Correct — smaller units means more of them fit, so the count rises even though the rope never changes.

options.label: Meters, because meters are bigger
options.feedback: Bigger units give a SMALLER count: fewer of them cover the same rope.

options.label: They are the same number
options.feedback: The length is the same, but the NUMBER differs because the units differ — 3 m and 300 cm.

options.label: It depends on the rope
options.feedback: It does not: for any length, the smaller unit always yields the larger count.

widget.prompt: A route measures 2 kilometers, and each kilometer is 1000 meters. Compute 2 × 1000.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding mixes a quantity with a rate. Each of the 2 kilometers contributes 1000 meters, so they multiply.
That divided. Going to the SMALLER unit needs more of them, so the number must grow.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the quantity and the conversion factor, then decide whether the count should grow or shrink.
